Article.ArticleTitle: Current Indications and Outcome of Pulmonary Resections of Tuberculosis Complications in Ibadan,Nigeria.

Abstract.AbstractText: To review the current indications and outcome of pulmonary resections for tuberculosis (TB) at the Cardiothoracic Surgery unit of the University College Hospital, Ibadan, Nigeria.

A retrospective case series of patients who had lung resections from January 2014 to January 2017 was performed. Data obtained from medical records included demographics, presenting symptoms, indication for surgery, preoperative evaluation and preparation, operative procedure, post-operative complications and follow up. Presence of TB in the patients was confirmed by detecting pathological changes suggestive of TB and/or had past history of pulmonary TB associated with its anatomical complications such as cavitation and bronchiectasis. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics.

Ten (10) patients had pulmonary resections during this study period. The median age was 33.5 years (range: 3-50). The indications for lung resection were massive or persistent haemoptysis and two patients also had aspergilloma. Six (6, 60%) patients had lobectomy, one a bilobectomy and remaining three a pneumonectomy. Complications included partial wound dehiscence in two patients (one of them had in addition postoperative empyema thoracis). One patient died immediately due to haemorrhage. Follow-up ranged from 6 to 37 months.

This study showed that the factors for the good outcome in patients presenting with massive or recurrent haemoptysis from tuberculosis complications were initial stabilisation and multi-disciplinary care. Hence, improved awareness of high standard care to encourage inclusion of patients with tuberculosis complications in surgical care protocol, as part of national control programmes is recommended.
